title: Top normal local cohomology classes and general residue transitions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Geometric points, costalks $R\Gamma_{\bar x}$, roots-of-unity twists, and immediate normalized residue transitions are as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. For every geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$ of finite codimension $c$ (the dimension of the reduced closure of $\bar y$ in the strict localization at $\bar x$), every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, and every $a\in\mathbf Z$, there are canonical maps
$$\operatorname{sp}^X_{\bar y,\bar x}:H^a(R\Gamma_{\bar y}M)\longrightarrow H^{a+2c}(R\Gamma_{\bar x}M(c)).$$
They are natural in $M$, agree with the normalized immediate transitions when $c=1$ and with the identity when $c=0$, commute with etale and strict-local restriction, and compose under chains of specializations, including the indicated Tate twists.

If $S$ is a Noetherian excellent normal strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $d$, with closed point $s$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], then
$$H^q_s(S,\Lambda(d))=0\quad(q>2d),\qquad [s]:\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d)).$$
The classes $[s]$ are invariant under the automorphisms of the chosen geometric points and commute with etale localization. On a normal integral excellent scheme, writing $r_x=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, the corresponding geometric classes $c_{\bar x}\in H^{2r_x}(R\Gamma_{\bar x}\Lambda(r_x))$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}(c_{\bar y})=c_{\bar x}$$
for every immediate geometric specialization, where $r_x=r_y+1$ and the source is twisted by $r_y$. At a geometric generic point the class is $1\in\Lambda$. Consequently the general specialization from a geometric generic point to $\bar x$ carries $1$ to $c_{\bar x}$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorems 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 and their proofs, especially 3.6.1 (invariance of the class); printed pp. 268, 277–280
